title: Watch List
markdown:
**What it is:** A set of external monitors that watch the outside world for you — stock tickers, RSS/Atom feeds, vendor status pages, SEC filings, web-search queries, and changes to specific web pages.

**What it does:**

- Say what to watch in your own words and check the plan before it starts, or set a monitor up by hand.
- Lists your monitors grouped by signal type, each card showing its target and when it last fired (or *Hasn't fired yet*). Click a group's heading to fold it.
- Pause or resume a monitor without deleting it.
- Let qualifying signals flow into your briefing as proposals — the same path as inbound email or Slack. Signals below a monitor's severity floor, or ones triage drops, never reach you.
- Review monitors the Executive suggests before they go live.
- Asks whether to make a monitor quieter when you keep dismissing its alerts.
- Edit the whole list from chat as well as here.

**How to use:**

1. Open **Work** in the sidebar and pick the **Watch list** tab. At the top, type what you want watched in **What should I watch?**, e.g. *"Tell me if Initech's stock moves more than 8%"* or *"Let me know when Globex posts about pricing"*, and click **Set it up**. Names of your competitors, vendors and tickers from your company profile are understood.
2. **Here's what I'll watch** shows the plan in four plain lines: what it watches, when it tells you, how often, and how loud. Nothing is saved yet.
   - **Start watching** adds it as shown.
   - **Change something** opens the form below with everything filled in, so you can adjust it and click **Add monitor**.
   - If it can't be watched (too vague, or a link that isn't public), it says why. Add a detail and try again.
3. To skip the plain-words step, open **Set it up by hand**. Fill in the **Signal type** and **Target** (see the table below), and optional **Name** and **Notes** (up to 500 characters). The rest is under **More options**, with defaults:
   - **Slug** — a short id in lowercase-with-dashes, e.g. `acme-pricing-page`. Left empty, it is named from the type and target. It must be unique.
   - **Trigger (JSON, optional)** — narrows what counts as a hit; leave blank for the defaults. The line under it says the trigger in words, e.g. *Tells you when: It moves 5% or more in a day, up or down.*
   - **Cadence** — `real_time`, `15min` (default), `hourly`, `daily` or `weekly`. It is stored with the monitor; how often a monitor is actually checked is set by its signal type (see the note below).
   - **Mode** — `active` (default) raises alerts; `dry_run` records signals without alerting, which is handy for trying out a noisy source.
   - **Severity floor / ceiling** — default `low` to `urgent`. Signals below the floor are logged but never become alerts.
4. Click **Add monitor**. An RSS / Atom target is checked first: it must load as a feed with entries. A URL that loads as a readable page with no feed is added as a **Page change** monitor instead; anything else is refused with the reason.
5. Use the switch on a card to pause or resume it. A paused monitor is not checked until you switch it back on.
6. Click the card (or **Open details** in its **⋯**) to open its page. There you can:
   - switch **When it fires** between **Alert me** (`active`) and **Shadow only** (`dry_run`);
   - see its **Configuration**: mode, cadence, severity range, specialist, how often it fired and was dismissed, its trust score, when it was last checked and last fired, when it tells you (the trigger in words, with the exact trigger under **Exact trigger**), and who added it;
   - edit **Notes** (saved when you click away);
   - read its **Recent signals**;
   - answer *"You dismissed 6 of the last 8 alerts from this. Only tell you about bigger changes?"* when most of its recent alerts were dismissed (at least 6 of the last 8). The first button makes it quieter: a stock monitor needs twice the move (5% becomes 10%); any other monitor's severity floor goes up one step. **Stop watching** opens the delete confirmation. **Keep as is** leaves it alone. Whichever you pick, it doesn't ask again until a new run of alerts is dismissed too;
   - delete it with **Delete monitor** in the **⋯** at the top, then **Delete** to confirm. Its past signals stay in the audit log.
7. A monitor the Executive added shows *added by the Executive* and has **Stop watching** choices in its **⋯**, each with a reason:
   - **not relevant** — removes it, and the Executive won't suggest that company or topic again;
   - **too noisy** — keeps it, but only high-severity signals get through;
   - **wrong source** — removes only this feed or page; the topic can still be watched another way.
8. Check **Suggested by the Executive** now and then. These are sources the research council thought worth watching but couldn't tie firmly enough to your company data to add on its own. Each card shows what it is about, which department it is for (that department's head was asked to review it), when it was suggested, and how many signals it has seen in shadow. **Approve** turns it on. The **⋯** has **Decline** with the same three reasons as **Stop watching**; declining as *too noisy* turns it on with only high-severity signals. Suggestions never alert until approved, and declines are remembered.

| Signal type | Target | Trigger example |
|---|---|---|
| Stock | Yahoo Finance ticker, e.g. `AAPL` | `{"abs_change_pct_gte": 5}` (default: 5% move) |
| RSS / Atom | Feed URL | `{"keywords": ["pricing", "launch"]}` |
| Vendor status | The status page's Atom/RSS feed URL | `{"keywords": ["degraded", "outage"]}` |
| SEC EDGAR | Ticker or CIK, e.g. `AAPL` or `320193` | `{"forms": ["8-K"]}` (default: 8-K, 10-K, 10-Q) |
| Page change | A public page URL | `{"keywords": ["price"]}` (default: any change) |
| Web search (billed) | A search query, e.g. `Acme Corp layoffs OR funding` | `{"keywords": ["acquisition"]}` |

**From chat:** *"Watch Apple stock and alert me on 5% moves."* · *"What are we watching right now?"* · *"Stop watching that competitor's blog, it's too noisy."* Chat is also the way to change a monitor's trigger, severity range or cadence after it's created; the page changes mode, notes and on/off, and the quieter-alerts question raises the trigger or severity floor.

*Note: each signal type is checked on its own schedule: vendor status pages every 5 minutes, stock prices every 15 minutes, RSS/Atom feeds every 30 minutes, SEC filings every hour, and page changes and web searches every 6 hours. Web-search monitors run a paid AI web search on every check, so use them sparingly.*
